digest.component_or_area: store git operations and local contention handling
propositions: Local rebar agents contend on shared git lock files (index.lock, HEAD.lock, packed-refs.lock) under high concurrent use; contention surfaces as errors to the agent instead of being silently absorbed via bounded retry.
Local-only git call sites lack uniform contention policy and have no or unbounded timeout bounds, leaving store operations and metrics vulnerable to stalls on wedged filesystems or peer lock holders.

A transient git lock conflict held briefly by a concurrent process should resolve silently after jittered backoff within a bounded budget (tens of seconds); only a permanently stuck lock should surface one actionable error naming the contended file and remedy.

Per-store advisory locking via fcntl, jittered exponential backoff with ref-lock signature retry, and watchdog timeouts on index-mutating and read-only git sites must route through a single seam so all call sites inherit the policy consistently.

Uncontended store git operations must incur no added latency; the advisory lock fast path is non-blocking and stale-lock reclamation remains index.lock-only with an age ceiling to prevent permanent wedge.
